chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of the Exalted: 'There is no good in most of their secret counsels except (in him) who enjoins charity or goodness.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He means by 'goodness', the loan.'
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'goodness' (ma'ruf) refer to in Quran 4:114 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this exegetical narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'good deed' (ma'ruf) permitting beneficial private counsel in Quran 4:114 specifically includes granting loans. This interpretation underscores the high spiritual status of financial generosity in Shia jurisprudence, linking economic transactions directly to divine reward and social welfare. By defining loan-giving as a form of ma'ruf, the Imam emphasizes that facilitating others' needs is a primary mechanism for earning merit beyond simple charity.
